articles.title: Trump says he will close historic DC golf course for 15 months of renovations
articles.summary: (AP) — President Donald Trump on Sunday announced plans to close a historic public golf course in the nation's capital for 15 months and redevelop it despite...
articles.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump on Sunday announced plans to close a historic public golf course in the nation's capital for 15 months and redevelop it despite a court challenge to his long-sought renovation.

Trump posted on social media about his intent to shutter the East Potomac Golf Course, not far from the White House, starting Nov. 15 to make it "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World."

A judge last week, however, ordered a halt to his redevelopment plans until at least Oct. 26 after scolding the government for starting a large-scale tree removal at the course over a holiday weekend while providing little notice to the court or the plaintiffs trying to stop the makeover.

Trump did not acknowledge the legal fight in his post, which included an artist's rendering for the course redesign.

"When completed, it will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments such as the U.S. Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup, and the Presidents Cup," Trump wrote.

Democracy Forward, which is representing the plaintiffs challenging his renovation plans, responded by saying that the course is part of a national park and recreation facility that is meant for everyone to enjoy.

"Our litigation is intended to protect this community jewel for the people and communities it serves and we will continue to work with our plaintiffs to defend it from unlawful and harmful intrusion," Skye Perryman, the president and CEO of the group, said in a statement.

The judge in the case took notice of Trump's online message and ordered the government to notify her by 8 p.m. EDT Sunday whether its position had changed from a court filing Friday that said "at most" Trump has given "preliminary thought" to the rebuilding plan and "there is no final agency action."

The government responded by repeating that "there is no final agency action" because the National Park Service has not completed its review and the plan is not final. The filing, signed by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, also said the government, in stating this position, had not been representing "the actual position or mental impressions" of Trump but instead had relied on his public statements.

Capital makeover extends well beyond the fairways

Trump, a golf aficionado who plays often, had already announced plans to makeover the links as part of his broader push to renovate and refurbish places around Washington , including the White House and the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Many of his projects, including plans for a huge ballroom at the White House, the installation of his own name on the Kennedy Center and construction of a massive arch , have been challenged in courts.

The 106-year-old park and course has been the subject of many emergency hearings as the president has sought to renovate it. While it has been open to Washingtonians of all income levels, opponents of Trump's plans to turn it into a high-end course have argued it will alter the character of the space and make it less affordable to people.

Trump in his post echoed arguments he has made to justify his plans to remake the Kennedy Center, arguing it is in such dangerous condition that it needs to close.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," Trump wrote.

Debris from the demolition of the White House East Wing to make way for his ballroom project has also been dumped on the grounds. The National Park Service has said the debris tested positive for lead, chromium and other toxic metals.

Trump also sought to justify the National Park Service's removal of hundreds of trees that the judge paused, writing in his announcement that when the golf course was originally built, "it was famous for no trees, with views of Washington, D.C., for all to see, but now, it is completely overgrown, dysfunctional, and unsafe."

Legal case returns to court and the administration seeks to remove the judge

Trump's post outlining a clear plan for construction complicates a federal court hearing scheduled for Monday in a lawsuit filed by the DC Preservation League and two golfers opposing the construction.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes has ordered key members of the Republican administration to testify on the recent tree-cutting and whether those actions are tied to the president's plans for the historical public links.

The administration on Friday asked for Reyes to be replaced on the case, questioning her impartiality and citing what it called "egregious" behavior from the bench in response to an emergency hearing Oct. 12. Her frustration boiled over in a three-hour hearing when she lambasted the government's attorney for the lack of notification she and the plaintiffs received before the trees were chopped down.

At the upcoming hearing, the judge is expected to address the request that she step aside. Meanwhile, over the weekend the plaintiffs asked that she grant them a more long-standing preliminary injunction in the case and/or a stay.

Associated Press writer Gary Fields in Washington contributed to this report.

articles.title: Quem são os senadores eleitos em 2026? | G1
articles.standfirst: Os dois candidatos mais votados em cada estado no primeiro turno das eleições 2026 foram eleitos para mandatos de oito anos. Cada eleitor votou em dois nomes para o cargo.
articles.summary: Os dois candidatos mais votados em cada estado no primeiro turno das eleições 2026 foram eleitos para mandatos de oito anos. Cada eleitor votou em dois nomes para o cargo.
articles.body:
As eleições de 2026 colocaram em disputa 54 vagas no Senado — duas por estado e duas pelo Distrito Federal. Isso significa a renovação de dois terços das 81 cadeiras da Casa.

Os dois candidatos mais votados em cada estado foram eleitos para mandatos de oito anos. Cada eleitor votou em dois nomes para o cargo.

Senadores eleitos em 2026 — Foto: Arte/g1

Veja os resultados completos das eleições

O g1 reúne em uma página especial os resultados oficiais das eleições de 2026 em todo o país. Com dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), os leitores podem consultar como ficou a votação para presidente da República, governadores, senadores, deputados federais e deputados estaduais e distritais em cada estado brasileiro.

A ferramenta também permite verificar o desempenho dos candidatos por unidade federativa e acessar mapas e painéis com os números consolidados da votação em todo o país.

articles.title: Flávio vê otimismo na reta final, mas alerta campanha após ruído sobre Bolsa Família | G1
articles.body:
Dentro da campanha do candidato do Partido Liberal (PL) à Presidência, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), o clima é de otimismo a cinco dias do segundo turno.

O candidato alerta, porém, para erros nesta reta final, como a confusão provocada por declarações de sua coordenadora econômica, Daniella Marques , sobre mudanças nas regras do Bolsa Família em um eventual governo do PL.

A avaliação é que qualquer tropeço pode impactar as intenções de voto nos últimos dias da eleição.

A campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) já está explorando politicamente as declarações de Daniella Marques ( entenda mais abaixo ).

Em entrevista à CBN Bahia, Daniella afirmou que em um eventual governo Flávio Bolsonaro pretende estabelecer uma regra de transição de dois anos para beneficiários que consigam emprego com carteira assinada ou abram o próprio negócio, com retorno automático ao programa caso a iniciativa não dê certo.

A declaração abriu espaço para que aliados de Lula passassem a divulgar a versão de que Flávio diz publicamente que não pretende mudar o Bolsa Família, enquanto sua equipe prepara alterações no programa.

Atualmente, o Bolsa Família já possui uma regra de proteção para famílias que registram aumento de renda. Pelas normas atuais, a permanência temporária no programa depende da renda por pessoa da família, da data de entrada na regra de proteção e do tipo de renda recebida.

O episódio ocorreu no mesmo período em que o governo Lula anunciou a antecipação para esta semana do pagamento dos benefícios de outubro, o primeiro com o reajuste de 15%.

Mais da metade dos beneficiários receberia apenas na próxima semana. Com a mudança, terão o crédito em suas contas antes do segundo turno da eleição presidencial.

Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro reconhecem que Daniella Marques não apresentou uma proposta inteiramente nova sobre a transição de beneficiários que aumentam a renda, mas avaliam que qualquer declaração mal colocada neste momento gera ruídos e munição para a campanha de Lula.

Isso ganha peso especialmente em uma disputa considerada acirrada.

"Estamos à frente do Lula, com dois a três pontos de diferença no mínimo, então não podemos colocar em risco essa vantagem nos últimos dias", diz um integrante do comando da campanha do senador do PL.

No início da tarde desta terça, o presidente gravou um vídeo nas redes sociais falando sobre o programa e as declarações da equipe do adversário.

Segundo ele, a equipe de Flávio Bolsonaro estaria trabalhando para agradar os adversários e acabar com o Bolsa Família.

Enquanto isso, na campanha de Lula, o clima é de apreensão. A avaliação interna é que a eleição está empatada e qualquer um dos dois candidatos pode vencer no próximo domingo, dia 25 de outubro.

"Conseguimos empatar, mas precisamos ultrapassar, e sabemos que tudo vai depender dos últimos dias de campanha", diz um integrante da campanha do petista.

Segundo ele, o lado positivo em comparação com o primeiro turno é que agora há uma grande mobilização em torno da candidatura do presidente Lula.

"Saímos de um clima de derrota no primeiro turno para um ambiente de que temos condições de ganhar no segundo turno", completa o aliado de Lula.

Cadastro do Bolsa Família e BPC para quem mora sozinho pode ser atualizado sem visita em casa em Salvador — Foto: Governo Federal

articles.title: No Maranhão, Lula diz que disputa pela última vez a Presidência e promete mandato ‘histórico’ | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato à reeleição afirmou em São Luís que, se vencer, pretende ampliar o Pé-de-Meia, criar benefício para universitários, gerar empregos e investir nas indústrias digital, verde e criativa.
articles.summary: Candidato à reeleição afirmou em São Luís que, se vencer, pretende ampliar o Pé-de-Meia, criar benefício para universitários, gerar empregos e investir nas indústrias digital, verde e criativa.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou nesta terça-feira (20) que esta será sua última campanha à Presidência da República e disse que pretende fazer de um eventual novo mandato um período “histórico”. A declaração foi dada durante campanha no Maranhão.

“Essa é a minha última campanha para presidente da República, última campanha. E esse mandato quero que seja histórico”, afirmou Lula.

No discurso, Lula afirmou que pretende, em um eventual novo mandato, ampliar o Pé-de-Meia, criar uma versão do programa para universitários, gerar empregos, formar profissionais e investir nas indústrias digital, verde e criativa.

A proposta de um Pé-de-Meia voltado a universitários já havia sido anunciada pelo presidente durante a campanha ( leia mais abaixo ).

Segundo a proposta apresentada pela campanha, seriam contemplados estudantes de universidades federais e estaduais e do ProUni.

A declaração de que esta será sua última campanha presidencial reforça algo que Lula já havia sinalizado no lançamento de sua candidatura à reeleição.

➡️Lula está com 80 anos e faz aniversário dois dias depois do segundo turno, que está marcado para 25 de outubro.

“Eu não vou ter chance de disputar o penta porque resolvi que, depois de a gente entregar o Brasil perfeitamente para o povo brasileiro, nós vamos sair de férias para namorar mais uns 20 anos”, disse na ocasião.

O petista já foi eleito presidente três vezes, em 2002, 2006 e 2022, e hoje exerce seu terceiro mandato à frente do Palácio do Planalto. Caso seja reeleito, governará o país pela quarta vez.

Presidente Lula cumpre agenda de campanha com caminhada no Centro de São Luís — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

No ato desta terça, Lula também agradeceu aos apoiadores no Maranhão e disse deixar o estado convencido de que vencerá os adversários.

“Quero agradecer por essa manifestação. Saio daqui convencido que vamos dar novamente uma surra nos bolsonaristas.”

Lula afirmou ainda que considera que os maranhenses reconhecem os investimentos realizados em seu governo no estado.

O presidente disse que, após São Luís, seguiria para Juazeiro e Petrolina e que manteria atividades de campanha até o dia da votação.

“Eu saio daqui e vou para Juazeiro, Petrolina, e só vamos parar no dia 25 de outubro, quando o 13 sair vitorioso nas urnas.”

Mais cedo, em pronunciamento em São Luís, Lula também falou de medidas anunciadas por seu governo na reta final da campanha.

O presidente afirmou que vai sancionar nesta quarta (21) o projeto que amplia o limite de faturamento dos microempreendedores individuais (MEIs) e perdoa dívidas de inadimplentes da categoria.

O texto foi aprovado pelo Senado na quinta (15) e seguiu para sanção presidencial. A proposta concede anistia integral aos MEIs inadimplentes e amplia o teto de faturamento da categoria.

“Amanhã [quarta] eu vou sancionar a lei de perdão da dívida do MEI. São 4 milhões de pessoas que tinham dívida ativa na União. Nós resolvemos anistiar para limpar o nome dessas pessoas no Serasa e poderem começar uma vida nova”, afirmou Lula.

O presidente também falou sobre o fim da escala de trabalho 6x1. A emenda constitucional que estabelece dois dias de descanso remunerado por semana foi promulgada pelo Congresso na sexta (16).

Lula ainda voltou a defender transporte público gratuito aos sábados e domingos.

“A gente vai então garantir, sábado e domingo, transporte público gratuito para que o povo possa passear nesses dois dias da semana.”

Na semana passada, Lula afirmou que enviaria ao Congresso uma Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) para garantir tarifa zero no transporte coletivo aos fins de semana em todas as cidades do país que oferecem o serviço.

Segundo o presidente, a proposta prevê o uso de recursos de emendas parlamentares.

Em São Luís, Lula também falou nesta terça sobre a disputa com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), seu adversário no segundo turno, em torno da divulgação de sigilos.

“Meus advogados estão lá em Brasília, no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, entregando um documento meu pedindo a quebra do sigilo bancário e telefônico e exigindo que o Flávio Bolsonaro faça o mesmo. O meu, dos meus filhos e da Janja”, afirmou Lula.

O petista também cobrou a divulgação dos dados de familiares do adversário.

“E que ele faça também da família dele. Até do pai dele que está preso. E ele entre na Justiça autorizando quebrar o sigilo, porque eu estou disposto a que a sociedade brasileira saiba quem é que é ladrão neste país, quem é que é corrupto. Eu quero ver se ele tem coragem de abrir o sigilo bancário dele”, afirmou.

No debate da Band, no domingo (18), Flávio Bolsonaro afirmou não ter “absolutamente nada a esconder”, mas não disse se autorizaria a divulgação de seus sigilos.

O ato no Centro Histórico de São Luís integra a agenda de reta final de Lula antes do segundo turno, marcado para domingo (25).

articles.title: Lula protocola documento no TSE e no STF em que diz que libera a divulgação de sigilos dele e de parentes se Flávio também o fizer | G1
articles.standfirst: Na manifestação, petista diz estar disposto a divulgar sigilos da esposa e dos cinco filhos, incluindo Lulinha, que é alvo de apurações da PF. Mas Lula condiciona o ato à divulgação de dados de Flávio, que é investigado em inquéritos no STF.
articles.summary: Na manifestação, petista diz estar disposto a divulgar sigilos da esposa e dos cinco filhos, incluindo Lulinha, que é alvo de apurações da PF. Mas Lula condiciona o ato à divulgação de dados de Flávio, que é investigado em inquéritos no STF.
articles.body:
O candidato do PT à reeleição, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , protocolou nesta terça-feira (20) um documento no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) em que afirma que autoriza a liberação de seus sigilos bancário, fiscal e eletrônico relativos aos últimos 8 anos , e também os de seus parentes, desde que o seu adversário na disputa presidencial, Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ), faça o mesmo.

Lula tomou a medida após desafiar Flávio, no debate realizado pela Band no último domingo (18), a divulgar os sigilos. O petista reiterou o desafio durante entrevista concedida nesta segunda-feira (19), em Porto Alegre (RS), onde cumpriu agenda de campanha.

Nesta terça, durante entrevista em São Luís (MA), Lula comentou o envio do documento ao TSE.

"Eu estou disposto a que a sociedade brasileira saiba quem é ladrão nesse país, quem é corrupto. Vamos ver se ele [Flávio] tem coragem de abrir a vida secreta dele", disse o candidato do PT à reeleição.

O presidente também apresentou uma manifestação com o mesmo teor ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

No debate da Band, Flávio afirmou não ter "absolutamente nada a esconder", mas não afirmou se vai autorizar a quebra do sigilo .

De acordo com a petição apresentada pela defesa de Lula ao TSE, a liberação e a ampla divulgação dos dados – seja por meio do sistema Divulga CandContas da Corte Eleitoral, ou de outro site de acesso público – vão abranger os seguintes familiares de Lula:

Rosângela Lula da Silva , a Janja, esposa do presidente;

Fábio Luís Lula da Silva , o Lulinha, filho que é alvo de investigações da PF ;

Os filhos de Lula já manifestaram que estão de acordo com a liberação dos dados.

O texto também estende a liberação de sigilos de empresas das quais os candidatos sejam sócios, administradores ou em cujas contas bancárias figurem como responsáveis financeiros ou "usuários master".

No caso de Lula, foi citada a empresa L.I.L.S. Palestras, Eventos e Publicações Ltda ., da qual é sócio não administrador.

🔎A expressão "usuário master", utilizada pela defesa de Lula de forma irônica no documento, é uma referência a reportagens que apontam que Flávio foi cadastrado como 'usuário master' em uma conta bancária de uma empresa pertencente ao advogado Willer Tomaz , investigado por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro.

A defesa de Lula propõe a divulgação pública dos dados bancários, fiscais e telefônicos de ambos os candidatos antes da próxima quarta-feira (21). Para os advogados, a medida é fundamental para assegurar que a população brasileira seja devidamente informada e possa decidir o seu voto.

Éden Valadares, secretário da campanha do petista, afirmou que a medida proposta por Lula tem respaldo na Constituição, que preza pela probidade administrativa, moralidade e prevê a análise de vida pregressa para o exercício de mandatos.

"Lula toma uma iniciativa histórica, que risca no chão a diferença dos candidatos, dando transparência a todo o seu sigilo e desafia o adversário a fazer o mesmo. Quem não deve, não teme", disse Valadares.

A petição apresentada ao TSE foi distribuída, por sorteio, ao ministro André Mendonça , que será o relator desse caso.

Lula condiciona a liberação dos seus sigilos e os de parentes à autorização, por Flávio Bolsonaro, da divulgação dos sigilos dele e dos seguintes familiares:

E também das seguintes empresas ligadas ao candidato do PL:

Flávio Bolsonaro Sociedade Individual de Advocacia ;

Bravo Grafeno Tecnologia e Inovação Ltda ;

Alcazar Holdings , empresa de propriedade de Willer Tomaz, que tem uma conta em que Flávio foi cadastrado como "usuário master" .

Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de dois inquéritos em tramitação no Supremo Tribunal Federal. Um deles, sobre lavagem de dinheiro, investiga a relação do candidato do PL com o advogado Willer Tomaz .

O outro inquérito trata do financiamento de "Dark Horse", uma cinebiografia sobre Jair Bolsonaro. Essa investigação apura negociações envolvendo recursos do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro , do Banco Master, para a produção do filme.

A defesa do senador tem negado irregularidades nas investigações, afirmando que não há envolvimento em ilícitos e criticando a divulgação de peças sigilosas durante o período eleitoral.

O presidente brasileiro Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, candidato do Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT) à reeleição, discursa durante um comício de campanha antes do segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, em Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brasil, em 19 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Vara

articles.title: Quem é o vice do Lula? | G1
articles.standfirst: Alckmin é o atual vice-presidente do Brasil e também foi ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços.
articles.summary: Alckmin é o atual vice-presidente do Brasil e também foi ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços.
articles.body:
Geraldo Alckmin e Lula posam após presidente votar em São Bernardo do Campo. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Geraldo Alckmin ( PSB ) é o candidato a vice-presidente do Brasil junto a Lula ( PT ).

Alckmin é o atual vice-presidente do Brasil e também foi ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços, assumindo os cargos em 1º de janeiro de 2023 na chapa de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Ele se afastou da pasta em 2026 para se dedicar à corrida pela reeleição.

Um dos fundadores do PSDB , Geraldo Alckmin, de 73 anos de idade, deixou o partido no final de dezembro de 2021 , após mais de três décadas. Na ocasião, afirmou que era um “tempo de mudança” e “hora de traçar um novo caminho”.

Formado em medicina, ele ingressou na política há 50 anos e, neste período, atuou em diversas funções: foi vereador, prefeito de Pindamonhangaba, deputado estadual, deputado federal, vice-governador e governador de São Paulo.

Alckmin disputou a Presidência da República duas vezes. Em 2006, quando perdeu no segundo turno para o ex-presidente Lula, e em 2018, quando ficou na quarta colocação, atrás de Jair Bolsonaro , Fernando Haddad e Ciro Gomes .

A migração de Alckmin para o PSB, neste ano, e o aceite para compor a chapa com Lula estiveram entre os principais acontecimentos da campanha eleitoral de 2022. O ex-prefeito de São Paulo Fernando Haddad e o ex-governador do estado Marcio França (PSB) foram os principais articuladores da aliança entre Alckmin e Lula .

articles.title: California residents accused by feds of voter fraud react with shock, confusion and anger
articles.summary: Several green card holders arrested in a Trump administration crackdown on alleged California voter fraud appeared in court Monday, with some saying they had...
articles.body:
At the federal courthouse in downtown Los Angeles late Monday, several green card holders arrested in a crackdown on alleged California voter fraud expressed confusion over the charges — with some saying they had no recollection of registering to vote, as Trump administration officials accuse them of doing.

Among them was Ana Domínguez, 60, a native of El Salvador living in Long Beach as a lawful permanent resident. Federal authorities accused her Monday of fraudulently registering to vote in July 2006 and then lying about it in her naturalization paperwork in March 2026.

Domínguez said she did not have any memory of registering to vote.

Another man accused of the same crimes as Domínguez said the same: He wasn't aware of ever registering to vote, as federal prosecutors claimed he had.

Both were among the 28 people charged with federal election-related crimes Monday, including fraudulent voter registration and making false statements in a naturalization application. Federal prosecutors and high-ranking Justice Department officials had touted the arrests during a news conference hours before as proof that California elections are corrupted by noncitizen voters — as President Trump has long alleged.

State officials said the isolated instances of noncitizens voting, if accurate, are not evidence of widespread voter fraud. They also raised questions as to whether the charges could be trusted to be accurate — citing similar accusations being disproved elsewhere in the country.

Election experts have said many instances of noncitizens registering to vote are a result of administrative error or confusion on the part of the immigrant — not intentional criminality.

"We know from past experience that sometimes people register to vote accidentally, as when there is a mistake at the DMV," Rick Hasen, director of the Safeguarding Democracy Project at UCLA School of Law, wrote Monday in a blog post. "There is only a crime if the government can prove willful violations of federal law."

Four of the defendants charged Monday had initial court appearances later that afternoon. Beforehand, more than a dozen of their loved ones milled around the federal courthouse in downtown L.A., antsy and clearly worried.

One woman, her baby and young daughter in tow, struggled to find the right courtroom. Another woman, Domínguez's daughter, cried in the hallway as she waited for her mother's case to get called up. When Domínguez moved to stand before the judge, she blew a kiss to her husband and daughter in the second row. She wore a black back brace and her legs were cuffed.

A third defendant — Omar Muñoz, 72, a lawful permanent resident from Belize whose arrest at his home in Commerce was captured by photographers in images transmitted around the world — shuffled into a court room shackled at the waist, his feet cuffed, still wearing the red and black pajama pants he'd been arrested in.

Muñoz was charged with fraudulently registering to vote in September 2019, and then voting in 2020, twice in 2022 and again in 2024. He is also accused of lying on his application to become a naturalized U.S. citizen, when he claimed to have never falsely claimed to be a U.S. citizen in the past.

In the courtroom, Muñoz held a hand over his heart as he waved to his family in the first row of the gallery.

Hasen, the UCLA expert, wrote that the government's blasting out images of Muñoz being arrested was clearly "meant to convey that the problem of noncitizen voting in California is both pervasive and serious, crimes that are undetected by willfully ignorant California election officials."

But the reality, he wrote, "is likely far different," with voter fraud limited to isolated cases, some with less nefarious intent.

First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, said Monday that the cases represent strong federal work to ensure that noncitizens aren't negating the votes of eligible U.S. voters — a problem he said California officials have refused to recognize despite federal authorities providing the proof.

Essayli dismissed the idea that those charged may have been unaware of what they were doing. "You have to go out of your way to register to vote; it's not something that just happens to you," Essayli said.

José Antonio Bañuelos-Díaz, 42, a Mexican national and West Adams resident, appeared in court wearing a reflective vest with the name of a landscaping company, blue jeans and boots with the American flag on them. He'd been on his way to work when he was arrested.

During the hearings, the defendants spoke only to acknowledge that they reviewed and understood the charges against them. In every case, the federal prosecutor said the government was not seeking detention.

The magistrate judge ordered the four released on personal recognizance and said they were not required to be under supervision. They are all set to appear in court for a preliminary hearing Nov. 9. Their deputy federal public defenders did not respond to a request for comment.

Lliani Orantes, Muñoz's daughter and a nurse who was born in the U.S., said her father had been hauled out of the family home by federal authorities after they swarmed and cordoned off the block. She said the family was rushing to figure out what happened, including whether Muñoz could have been confused with younger relatives of the same name, including a U.S.-born son who is a registered voter.

Orantes also expressed frustration with the handling of her father's arrest — to which federal authorities had clearly alerted some media, who were brought along for the raid.

She said that her father is recovering from cervical surgery, rotator cuff repair on a shoulder and a double knee replacement, and that he was pulled out of the family's home "like he was a dog" as part of what she described as a "political ploy, an example used for the operation" — which federal authorities dubbed "Operation Protect the Vote."

"They're trying to instill fear in society," she said.

"We have so much more in the world to be dealing with, do we really need to focus on these little things that could be taken care of in a different fashion? In a different way? Like, hey, somebody from immigration visit the home," she said.

California Atty. Gen. Rob Bonta — who is defending the state and top election officials for the state and Los Angeles County against a lawsuit from the Justice Department alleging they are not treating alleged voter fraud by noncitizens seriously enough — said Monday that voting illegally is wrong and "one-off, isolated incidents" of it should be prosecuted.

But Bonta denied that there is widespread voter fraud in the state, called 28 cases brought out of the 23 million registered voters in California a "drop in the bucket," and said he'd be watching how those cases play out in court.

"We'll see what the facts show, and whether they'll have to drop charges or whether they'll be able to prosecute," he said.

About 3 p.m. Monday, the four defendants at the downtown courthouse were released and exited the courtroom, some to family members waiting in the hallway to hug them.

Domínguez wiped away tears as she recounted her arrest, showing bruises on her wrists from the handcuffs.

"They were accusing me of voter fraud since 2006," she said. Domínguez said the accusations don't even make sense considering she has never voted.

"If I would have committed all those frauds about voting registration and whatever they're saying, since 2006, wouldn't you imagine that I would have been voting all these other years?" she asked.

In a visual presentation at their news conference, federal authorities alleged that 21 of the 28 people charged had actually voted. Domínguez was not one of them.

Domínguez said she's been a lawful permanent resident since the late 1980s, and that she applied for U.S. citizenship earlier this year. As part of the application process, she said she told an immigration agent that the only people registered to vote in her household were her husband, who previously became a U.S. citizen, and her daughter, who was born in the country.

Since then, Domínguez said, she has just been waiting on the citizenship ceremony, "but it never came through."

Instead, she was arrested Monday when she was about to leave for work as an administrative assistant.

"I never, ever in my entire life ... thought this would ever happen to me," she said.

Muñoz and his family gathered outside the courthouse. Muñoz, who declined to comment on the charges against him, said he'd been up to have coffee early that morning when he heard the commotion outside. Agents said if he didn't open the door, they'd break it down.

He described seeing helicopters, at least eight cars and several agents from different agencies descending on his home, and recalled thinking, "What movie am I in?"

"That's a lot of money. Taxpayers paying for that," he said. "They could have sent me a letter saying report to the court."

Muñoz — who said he came to the U.S. legally in 1975 and has "paid all my taxes" since — said he explained to the arresting agents that he'd had six surgeries recently and they "didn't care." He said he didn't learn about the charges against him until four hours later.

Muñoz's son, Omar Muñoz Jr., questioned why federal agents didn't take his father's age and ailments into consideration.

"We understand that there's a procedure that has to be addressed at court. But 5 in the morning, handcuffed? It's just the way everything was done, and what my mom had to go through. It's not just an impact on my father's health, but also on my mom," he said. "There is a law, we understand that. But innocent until proven guilty."

Muñoz's wife, Esmeralda, echoed her son's questions about why so many agents were deployed to their home.

"Seriously? All these people just to come for an elderly person," she said she told a federal agent. "It's unbelievable."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Fact check: Trump brings back his 2024 lie that schools are secretly sending kids to hospitals for gender surgery
articles.summary: In the final months of the 2024 presidential campaign, President Donald Trump told an outlandish lie that schools in parts of the US were sending children fo...
articles.body:
In the final months of the 2024 presidential campaign, President Donald Trump told an outlandish lie that schools in parts of the US were sending children for gender surgeries without the knowledge of their parents.

Trump has now revived the lie for the final weeks of the 2026 midterm campaign.

At a rally in Georgia on Friday, he said , "We got critical race theory and transgender mutilization (sic) insanity out of our schools. I mean, we have five states where your child goes off to school as Tim and comes back as Tammy, three or four days later. It's true. And teachers make – somebody makes a decision. Can you imagine? 'Goodbye, Timmy. I love you so much. I'll see you later.' And you say, 'Where's my son? My son is in the hospital.' Can you imagine? Can you imagine? They don't even need approval. It's sick. You'll have five – I think Minnesota and some others – I think it's five or six states. You know that, right?"

There is no state in which schools would not need parental approval to send a child to a hospital for elective surgery. And just like in 2024 , experts in gender identity care told CNN that they do not know of a single case in which a US school had secretly sent a child away for gender surgery.

The White House itself couldn't provide one example proving Trump's claim. Five conservative organizations we contacted in search of any examples did not respond.

A spokesperson for Minnesota's education department, Anna Arkin, called Trump's claim "unequivocally false." And the president of the National Association of School Nurses board of directors, Lynn Nelson , noted Monday that "even giving a student Tylenol typically requires written parent or guardian permission and, in many jurisdictions, an order from a licensed health care provider." Nelson said Trump's claims about schools sending children off for secret gender surgeries are "false" and "misrepresent the care school nurses provide."

"There are no documented cases of schools taking children to hospitals for gender-affirming surgery," said Landon Hughes , an instructor at Harvard Medical School who has published studies on the prevalence of gender care among US minors. "This claim is not only entirely unsupported by evidence but also reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the legal and medical consent requirements governing surgical care for minors."

"I know of no such case, and it is extremely difficult to envision a scenario where that would happen," said Lindsey Dawson , director of the LGBTQ Health Policy Program at KFF, a health policy research organization. "Schools are very limited in the type of care they can provide without parental consent."

Dawson also said, "The claim that schools are medically transitioning students is patently false. Transgender people make up a small share of the population, not all transgender people pursue medical transition, and surgery among young people is extremely rare. It is certainly not happening in schools or because of school policy."

The limited available data suggests a tiny percentage of transgender people receive surgery as minors and that the vast majority of the gender surgeries that minors do receive are chest procedures between the ages of 15 and 17 .

Some states ban people under 18 from receiving gender surgery in particular or both gender surgery and broader gender identity care like hormones and puberty-blocking drugs. Even in states where these medical interventions are legal for minors, parental consent is required, Dr. Laura Taylor , medical director of the Gender-Affirming Care Program at the University of Southern California, said in 2024.

Taylor outlined a lengthy process before a minor might undergo such a surgery.

"In adolescents, the decision to start hormones and/or have surgery would happen after consultation with an interdisciplinary team for a psychosocial assessment," she said, the bold type hers. "The assessment includes understanding the dysphoria related to gender incongruence (the distress caused by the physical characteristics that do not match the person's identity), how long it has been present, excluding other reasons to account for the dysphoria, and making sure the adolescent and family can provide informed consent."

The White House couldn't find any examples proving Trump's point

Trump has started peppering his speeches with his tale about schools and clandestine surgeries, delivering vague versions at a Kansas rally on Monday, a Kentucky rally on Saturday and an Ohio rally on October 12 . But when we asked the White House this week for cases in which US schools had actually sent children to hospitals for gender surgeries without parental consent, Trump's team wasn't able to find any – let alone examples from the "five or six states" Trump invoked.

Instead, in an unsigned email on Monday, the White House sent along a list of cases in which schools facilitated minors' social transitions without their parents' knowledge – allowing them to be called a different name or pronouns at school – and sometimes allegedly connected these minors with counselors or therapists who also supported the social transitions.

That's very different than Trump's narrative about schools sending a child to a hospital for an operation their parents didn't know about.

The White House claimed in the unsigned email: "President Trump is clearly explaining that a direct nexus exists between these processes being initiated at schools, and the same kids eventually ending up in hospitals and doctors' offices taking dangerous drugs and undergoing permanent mutilation procedures."

Nope, Trump wasn't "clearly explaining" that argument. The president didn't say children "eventually" end up getting surgery; his story wasn't about the alleged future dangers of schools permitting minors to make social transitions.

Rather, for the second election cycle in a row, Trump simply asserted that schools in parts of the country have a permitted practice of sending children to be operated on when their parents thought they were attending class – and, for the second election cycle in a row , his aides couldn't prove that this had ever happened.

Most of the news articles the White House highlighted Monday did not mention surgery at all, though the White House used the word "mutilation" to describe cases involving only social transitions. And a case that did involve a mention of surgery did not end up in actual surgery – undermining, rather than confirming, Trump's stories.

In that case, Colorado parents said that after their daughter was experiencing feelings of depression, anxiety and "transgender identification" in her freshman year of high school, a school counselor encouraged her to make a social transition and discussed the possibility of hormone treatments and gender surgery. But a lawsuit filed by the parents said that after they "would not consent" to hormones or surgery, their daughter came to regret the social transition and resumed identifying as a girl.

In other words, even in a state known as being supportive of students who want to undergo social transitions at school, there was no surgery without parental consent.

articles.title: Ahead of elections, Bessent says a Democrat-led Congress could do little to stop Trump agenda
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 20 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that there was not much a Democrat-led House of Representatives could do t...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Oct 20 (Reuters) - US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that there was not much a Democrat-led House of ‌Representatives could do to stop the Trump administration's agenda.

"I think there's ‌very little," Bessent said in an interview on 2Way TV two weeks ahead of November's midterm ​elections.

"We have very durable tariff authorities," he said, referring to Democrats' opposition to Trump broadly imposing tariffs on goods imported from countries around the world.

Control of Congress is at stake as voters head to the polls on November ‌3 to choose members of ⁠the House of Representatives and Senate and governors in states across the country. The Republican Party currently has a ⁠narrow majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

The election comes as Trump's approval rating has dipped over his handling of the high cost ​of ​living for Americans during the US-Israeli war ​with Iran that has raised ‌fuel prices.

Bessent said the Treasury's effort to isolate Iran economically was working.

"We haven't seen any loadings at the Iranian oil facility on Kharg Island since August. Iran currently has no oil on the water," he said.

"Panic is starting to set in ... I don't know whether it's going to take ‌four more weeks or eight more weeks, ​but at a point, their economy will ​go nonlinear," he said.

Bessent also ​said he had not heard whether Russian President Vladimir ‌Putin had accepted Trump's invitation to ​attend the G20 summit ​in Florida in December.

"I haven't seen his RSVP yea or nay yet," Bessent said.

Trump has said Russia has agreed to supply diesel ​to global markets, and ‌his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed ​to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine.

(Reporting by ​Katharine Jackson; editing by Michelle Nichols)

articles.title: Katrin Ortega, la candidata del PSOE más votada en porcentaje en Málaga en 2023, abandona el partido: "No me representa este PSOE"
articles.standfirst: Katrin Ortega obtuvo el 88% de los votos en las elecciones municipales de 2023, el mayor porcentaje de apoyo al PSOE en la provincia
articles.summary: Katrin Ortega obtuvo el 88% de los votos en las elecciones municipales de 2023, el mayor porcentaje de apoyo al PSOE en la provincia
articles.body: Katrin Ortega, alcaldesa de Parauta, municipio de Málaga, ha anunciado su salida del PSOE por sus discrepancias con la dirección nacional de la formación. La regidora consiguió el 88% de los votos en las elecciones municipales de 2023, un resultado que convirtió su candidatura en la que obtuvo el mayor porcentaje de apoyo electoral para el PSOE en la provincia. Además, logró los siete concejales que componen la Corporación municipal. "Me marcho porque no me siento representada por el PSOE nacional actual", ha afirmado Katrin Ortega en declaraciones recogidas por Málaga Hoy. La alcaldesa de la localidad parauteña ha reconocido que se trata de una decisión que le produce tristeza, pero ha defendido que responde a la necesidad de actuar de forma coherente con sus convicciones. "Entiendo que aquel socialismo no es el actual, pero debería ser normal poder decir a tu partido que no estás de acuerdo con algo, igual que lo haces con tus padres o tus hermanos", ha señalado Katrin Ortega. La regidora ha insistido en que sus discrepancias políticas con la dirección nacional son el único motivo que la ha llevado a abandonar la formación. Katrin Ortega ha explicado que llevaba tiempo meditando su salida y que había compartido sus dudas con personas de su entorno. Aunque inicialmente tenía previsto abandonar el partido antes, finalmente decidió esperar después de recibir peticiones para que reconsiderara su decisión. Pese a su marcha del PSOE, la alcaldesa ha descartado dejar el cargo y continuará al frente del Ayuntamiento de Parauta. También seguirán en el equipo de gobierno los otros dos concejales que han solicitado la baja del partido. De este modo, los tres ediles pasarán a ser concejales no adscritos, mientras que el resto de integrantes de la candidatura municipal, que concurrían como independientes, mantendrán su situación. "Seguimos con normalidad y yo sigo en la Alcaldía; ahora la única diferencia es que pasamos a ser concejales no adscritos", ha explicado Katrin Ortega, que ha defendido la continuidad de la gestión municipal pese a su ruptura con el PSOE.
